steps.label: Do Now: The Accumulator (2 of 2)

Do Now: The Accumulator (2 of 2)

Recap of the last lesson. Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2022, Question 2(c). Type your answer, then press Submit answer (or Check my answer to have it marked). Done when you have marked it against the model answer.

items.prompt: Identify the component within the CPU that the accumulator is built into and describe the purpose of the accumulator.
scheme: It stores the result of interim calculations
items.guidance: One mark for the component: the arithmetic logic unit (ALU). Then any two from the purpose points, one mark each: it stores data temporarily; it stores the result of interim calculations. "It stores data" with no "temporarily" earns no mark for point 2.
items.modelAnswer: The ALU. It temporarily stores data. It stores the results of interim calculations.

walkthrough.title: Walk me through it: describe a register's purpose

steps.text: A similar question. "Describe the purpose of the program counter (PC)." It is worth 2 marks.
Point 1: what does it hold? The PC holds an address.
Point 2: which address? The address of the next instruction.
Check: two separate points, one mark each. "It holds things" alone would earn nothing: say exactly what.
steps.visual: holds an address + of the next instruction = 2 marks

steps.label: Buses and Data Movement
steps.content:
3.1 Computer Architecture

Buses and Data Movement

Year 10

  • Today: how values and messages travel between the CPU and memory, and why.
  • Three buses: what each one carries, and which way it goes.
  • How this lesson works: on each slide, read the question, predict by picking an answer, then read why. Then go to the next slide.

steps.label: Why the CPU Needs Buses
steps.content:
Why the CPU Needs Buses

What to do: read the two lines, look at the picture, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • The CPU and memory are separate parts. They are joined by wires.
  • A bus is a set of wires that carries signals between parts, such as the CPU and memory.
CPU
Address bus
Data bus
Control bus
Memory
AddressHolds
531
612
725
817

The three buses join the CPU and memory.

items.prompt: Predict: the CPU wants the number stored at address 6. What must the CPU send to memory?
options: Where the number is, and a message: read it
Nothing: memory knows what the CPU needs
items.explain: Memory only does what it is told. The CPU sends where (the address 6) and what to do (read). Then memory sends back what it holds there (12). Three different things travel, so there are three buses: the address bus, the data bus and the control bus.

steps.label: Your Note: Why Three Buses
steps.content:
Your Note: Why Three Buses

What to do: write each note in your book, in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea.

Note in your book: in your own words, explain WHY the CPU needs three buses, not one.Check my note

A model note: The CPU sends where (an address) and what to do (a signal), and the value travels too (data). These are three different things, so there are three buses.

steps.label: Which Way Does the Address Bus Go?
steps.content:
Which Way Does the Address Bus Go?

What to do: read the line, look at the picture, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • The address bus carries an address: the place in memory to read or write.
  • The CPU wants the value at address 6, so 6 goes on the address bus.
CPU
Address bus6 →
Data bus
Control bus
Memory
AddressHolds
531
612
725
817

The CPU sends the address 6.

items.prompt: Predict: memory never chooses which address the CPU uses. Which way does the address bus need to go?
options: Out of the CPU to memory only
Into the CPU from memory only
items.explain: Out of the CPU only. The CPU chooses the address and sends it to memory. Memory never needs to send an address back, so the address bus goes one way.

steps.label: Explain It: The Address Bus
steps.content:
Explain It: The Address Bus

Type your answer in your own words, then press Check my answer to have it marked, and Submit answer to see the model answer. Fix your answer, then copy your best version into your book.

items.prompt: In your own words: which way does the address bus carry an address, and WHY?
scheme: Out of the CPU to memory only (one way)
Because the CPU chooses the address // memory never needs to send an address back
items.guidance: One mark for the direction: out of the CPU to memory, or one way from the CPU. One mark for the reason: the CPU chooses or sends the address, or memory never sends an address back. "It goes one way" with no reason earns the first mark only.
items.modelAnswer: Out of the CPU only. The CPU chooses the address, so memory never sends one back.

steps.label: Which Way Does the Data Bus Go?
steps.content:
Which Way Does the Data Bus Go?

What to do: compare the two pictures, then pick your prediction. The reason appears under it.

  • The data bus carries data and instructions: the value itself.
CPU
Address bus6 →
Data bus12
Control bus
Memory

Read: the CPU wants the value at address 6. It holds 12.

CPU
Address bus8 →
Data bus42
Control bus
Memory

Write: the CPU stores 42 at address 8.

items.prompt: Predict: in the read, 12 travels on the data bus. In the write, 42 travels on the data bus. Which way must the data bus go?
items.explain: Both ways. In the read, 12 comes into the CPU from memory. In the write, 42 goes out of the CPU to memory. One bus does both jobs, so it must go both ways.

steps.label: Why the Control Bus Is Needed
steps.content:
Why the Control Bus Is Needed

What to do: read the lines, then pick a prediction for each question. The reason appears under each one.

  • The control bus carries control signals.
  • The control unit (CU) sends signals such as read and write.
  • Devices send signals too. The keyboard tells the CU: a key has been pressed.
CPU
Address bus6 →
Data bus
Control bus?
Memory

Address 6 is on its way. What else must memory be told?

items.prompt: Predict: the CPU sends address 6 to memory. How does memory know whether to send its value back or to store a new value?
options: A read or a write signal tells it
It looks at how big the number is
It always sends its value back
items.explain: The address only says where. The CU also sends a read or a write signal on the control bus, so memory knows what to do.

items.prompt: Predict: a key is pressed. The keyboard sends a signal to the CU. Which way does this signal go?
items.explain: Into the CPU. The CU sends signals out (read, write), and devices send signals in. So the control bus carries signals both ways.

steps.label: Check: Which Bus?
steps.content:
Check: Which Bus?

What to do: pick the bus for each question. Ask: is it a place, a value, or a command? Done when both are answered.

items.prompt: The CPU wants the value stored at address 9. Memory holds 25 there. Which bus carries the 9?
items.explain: 9 is the place in memory, so it is an address. Addresses go on the address bus.

items.prompt: The CPU wants memory to store a value. Which bus carries the write signal?
items.explain: Write is a command from the CU. Commands and signals go on the control bus.

steps.label: Your Notes: Data, Control and Which Bus
steps.content:
Your Notes: Data, Control and Which Bus

What to do: write each note in your book, in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea.

Note in your book: in your own words, explain WHY the data bus must go both ways. Use the word read and the word write.Check my note

A model note: In a read, the value comes into the CPU from memory. In a write, the value goes out of the CPU to memory. One bus does both, so it goes both ways.

Note in your book: in your own words, explain WHY memory needs a read or a write signal as well as the address.Check my note

A model note: The address only says where. The signal says what to do: send the value back (read) or store a new value (write).

Note in your book: explain WHY the 9 goes on the address bus, and not on the data bus.Check my note

A model note: 9 is a place in memory, so it is an address. The value stored there (25) is data, so it goes on the data bus.

steps.label: Activity 1: Which Bus, Which Way?
steps.content:
Activity 1: Which Bus, Which Way?

What to do: pick the bus for every row (from level 2, also which way it goes), then press Check. One check per round, and a mistake means the round does not count. Done when you have cleared level 2 (two clean rounds in a row at each level). The help gets less as you go up.

steps.label: Compare: A Read and a Write
steps.content:
Compare: A Read and a Write

What to do: the table shows what each bus carries in a read and in a write. Picture which way each one travels, then pick your prediction.

Read: the value at address 6 (it holds 12)Write: store 42 at address 8
Address bus68
Data bus1242
Control busReadWrite

items.prompt: Predict: which bus changes direction between the read and the write?
items.explain: Only the data bus. In both jobs the address and the read or write signal go out of the CPU. The value comes in for a read (12) and goes out for a write (42).

steps.label: Check: Which Way?
steps.content:
Check: Which Way?

What to do: pick the way for each question. Ask: where does it start, and where does it end up? Done when both are answered.

items.prompt: The CPU stores 30 at address 7. Which way does 30 travel on the data bus?
items.explain: 30 starts in the CPU and ends up in memory, so it goes out of the CPU.

items.prompt: The CPU wants the value at address 5. Which way does the address 5 travel?
items.explain: The CPU chooses the address and sends it to memory. An address only ever goes out of the CPU.

steps.label: Explain It: A Write
steps.content:
Explain It: A Write

Type your answer in your own words, then press Check my answer to have it marked, and Submit answer to see the model answer. Fix your answer, then copy your best version into your book.

items.prompt: The CPU stores 19 at address 4. In your own words, say what each bus carries and which way it goes. Then explain WHY the data bus goes that way.
scheme: Address bus: carries 4 (the address), out of the CPU to memory
Control bus: carries a write signal, out of the CPU (from the CU) to memory
Data bus: carries 19 (the value), out of the CPU to memory
Because in a write the value starts in the CPU and ends up in memory
items.guidance: One mark for each point. Points 1 to 3 need both what the bus carries and the direction. Point 4 needs the reason (the value starts in the CPU, or is going to be stored in memory). A bus with the wrong value or direction earns no mark for that point.
items.modelAnswer: Address bus: 4, out to memory. Control bus: write, out to memory. Data bus: 19, out to memory, because the value starts in the CPU and is stored in memory.

steps.label: Your Notes: A Read and a Write
steps.content:
Your Notes: A Read and a Write

What to do: write each note in your book, in your own words. Then press Check my note and compare. Fix your note if it misses an idea.

Note in your book: explain WHY a read signal goes on the control bus, and not on the data bus.Check my note

A model note: A read signal is a command from the CU, not a value. Commands go on the control bus.

Note in your book: explain WHY only the data bus changes direction between a read and a write.Check my note

A model note: The address and the read or write signal always start in the CPU. The value starts in memory for a read, and in the CPU for a write.

steps.label: Activity 2: Trace a Read and a Write
steps.content:
Activity 2: Trace a Read and a Write

What to do: for each bus, pick what it carries and which way it goes, for a read and a write. One check per round, and a mistake means the round does not count. Done when you have cleared level 4, where there is no help.

steps.label: Exam Question: Two Other Buses
steps.content:
Exam Question: Two Other Buses

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/11, November 2022, Question 2(a). Phil has a computer that is designed using the Von Neumann model. Type your answer, then press Submit answer (or Check my answer to have it marked). Done when you have marked it against the model answer.

items.prompt: One type of component within the CPU is an address bus. Identify two other types of bus and state what each is responsible for transmitting in the CPU.
scheme: ... responsible for transmitting data or instructions
items.guidance: One mark for each correct bus (max 2) and one mark for the matching description of what it transmits. A description earns its mark only next to the matching bus. The address bus is in the question, so it earns no mark.
items.modelAnswer: Data bus: transmits data and instructions. Control bus: transmits control signals.

steps.label: Exam Question: The Control Bus
steps.content:
Exam Question: The Control Bus

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/12, March 2021, Question 8(b)(ii). Type your answer, then press Submit answer (or Check my answer to have it marked). Done when you have marked it against the model answer.

items.prompt: Describe the role of the control bus.
scheme: It carries or transfers control signals (or commands)
... from the CPU or CU to components, or from devices to the CPU or CU
To synchronise the cycle the CPU carries out
items.guidance: Any two, one mark each. Point 2 follows point 1. "It controls the computer" earns no mark.
items.modelAnswer: It carries control signals from the CU to other components.

steps.label: Exam Question: One Bus and Its Purpose
steps.content:
Exam Question: One Bus and Its Purpose

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13, June 2023, Question 2(c)(ii). The fetch-decode-execute cycle is the next lesson. For now, name a bus and explain what it carries. Type your answer, then press Submit answer (or Check my answer to have it marked). Done when you have marked it against the model answer.

items.prompt: The CPU contains registers and buses. Identify one bus that can be found in the CPU and explain its purpose in the fetch-decode-execute cycle.
scheme: Names a bus: address bus, data bus or control bus
It transmits or carries addresses (address bus), data (data bus) or control signals (control bus)
... between components in the CPU (for the control bus: from the control unit to other components)
items.guidance: One mark for the correct name of a bus. Two marks for the matching description: what it carries (point 2) and where (point 3). The description must match the bus named.
items.modelAnswer: Address bus. It carries addresses between components in the CPU.

steps.label: Exam Questions: Which Part Uses the Bus?
steps.content:
Exam Questions: Which Part Uses the Bus?

Cambridge IGCSE 0478/13 June 2021 Q10(a) and 0478/11 November 2021 Q6(a), one row of each table. What to do: pick the component each statement applies to.

items.prompt: Uses the data bus to send data into or out of the CPU.
items.explain: RAM is outside the CPU. It sends data into the CPU, and receives data out of it, on the data bus.

items.prompt: It uses the address bus to send an address to another component.
items.explain: The MAR holds the address memory is about to read or write, and sends it out on the address bus.

steps.label: Notes Check: Your WHY Notes
steps.content:
Notes Check: Your WHY Notes

What to do: look in your book. You should have each note below, in your own words. Missing one? Go back to the slide named, write it, and press Check my note. Then go to the next slide.

  • WHY there are three buses, not one. Slide: Your Note: Why Three Buses.
  • Which way the address bus goes, and WHY. Slide: Explain It: The Address Bus.
  • WHY the data bus goes both ways, using read and write. WHY memory needs a read or a write signal. WHY an address is not data. Slide: Your Notes: Data, Control and Which Bus.
  • A write, bus by bus, and WHY the data bus goes out. Slide: Explain It: A Write.
  • WHY a read signal goes on the control bus. WHY only the data bus changes direction. Slide: Your Notes: A Read and a Write.
